keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m measured as the distance to the closest point of the Earth's surface — not simply straight down, so near a slope the terrain beside you can also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the entity responsible for it may request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or can transfer more than 80 J of impact energy) — this applies even to toys. Below 250 g, registration is still mandatory if the drone carries a sensor capable of capturing personal data, unless it is considered a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are separate and depend on the drone's class and subcategory.

In Spain, the minimum age under RD 517/2024 (art. 7) is 12 years for C0 drones in subcategory A1, and 14 years for C1/C2 and A3 without direct supervision; in both cases, completing the online A1/A3 training and exam is required.

Flights in urban environments or over assemblies of people: UAS operators subject to the registration obligation must notify the Ministerio del Interior in advance, at least five calendar days before the planned start date of the operation (art. 40 of RD 517/2024).

In the open category, you must keep the drone within your own direct visual line of sight, with the naked eye (corrective glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the help of an observer, maintaining clear and effective communication between you at all times, so that together you can monitor the airspace and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.
Observe the UAS no-fly zones around airports and airfields (RD 517/2024) — always check the ENAIRE Drones map.
Night flights are permitted in the open category—the drone must be equipped with a visible flashing green light.
National parks require express permission from park authorities
Canary Islands and Balearic Islands: Additional local restrictions may apply
importantNotes: Third-party liability insurance is mandatory at EU level for drones over 20 kg; many Member States—including Spain—also require it for the A2 subcategory and the specific and certified categories. It is not usually mandatory at EU level for A1/A3 below 20 kg, although it is advisable to check the current national regulations.
Registration with AESA is free and valid in all EU/EASA countries
Fines range from €60 to €225,000 depending on the severity of the offense (Air Safety Law 21/2003).
Military bases and government buildings: absolute no-fly zones
The GDPR applies when capturing identifiable images
